mathematical_assessments.assessment: The small-matrix commutator contraction gives nilpotence; the compact-stabilizer finite-cover prefix deletion gives finite index without a finite-volume hypothesis. The nontrivial nilpotent core centralizer forces elementary translations or a cyclic loxodromic group. Explicit displacement formulas identify full components, uniform closure separation and locally finite closed lifts. Quotient embedding and properness retain arbitrary infinitely generated groups and both parabolic ranks.

Compactness of the rank-one parabolic quotient bounds the transverse imaginary coordinate, and the ball formula enlarges width by Y sinh(epsilon). The stated integrals give ell R/T^2 + 2 ell sinh(epsilon)/T and a/(2T^2) exactly. Quotient image volume is bounded by source volume even below the precisely invariant level. Finite compact truncation sheets and lowered cusp caps cover the complete convex neighborhood.

The elementary complex Shimizu recursion proves the stated bound. Its application to shortest parabolics separates the larger displacement horoballs; halving displacement raises heights by two and gives 2 log(2) separation. Ideal points of the closed Dirichlet domain cannot be conical. Bounded-parabolic rank-one strips and rank-two Dirichlet lattice inequalities bound all horizontal coordinates, excluding ideal accumulation of the truncated Dirichlet-convex intersection at each parabolic point. Thus the actual truncated convex quotient is compact. Boundary horoball intersections in C give positively separated quotient points, so compactness forces finitely many cusp orbits; the cap supplier then proves every-radius volume finiteness.

Packing equal embedded balls only in the closed thick part of the convex quotient proves its compactness. Rank-two parabolics are bounded by a lattice parallelogram; an unbounded rank-one transverse limit set would give infinitely many disjoint same-radius balls at one fixed height in a precisely invariant horoball, contradicting the actual convex-neighborhood volume assumption. A convex ray either returns to a compact set, stays in a compact-quotient loxodromic tube, or tends to the base of one horoball. No finite total quotient volume or torsion-order bound is imported.

Normalized matrix convergence is proved on the sphere and compactified Hermitian model. A conical orbit sequence yields the two distinct boundary limits; conversely two other limit points give two geodesics whose common bounded-neighborhood escaping orbit can accumulate only at the proposed conical point. Equivariant limit-set HOMEOMORPHISMS therefore preserve conicality. Parabolic type is detected by one versus two fixed points on the actual limit set, and the stabilizer quotient homeomorphism preserves boundedness. Both locally proved GF directions then give the precise volume and truncation consequences. The whole-sphere conjugacy clause separately identifies the limit set as the complement of the maximal properly discontinuous open set; no interior extension is assumed.

Finite factor-word reductions and the open-pair interaction give faithfulness, including the exact factor intersection. The properness hypothesis supplies one fixed omitted point p in an open partner set even when the difference itself has empty interior. After removing odd-length words or inverting, every possible identity-convergent even-word sequence omits that same p; inverse convergence contradicts this. Cyclic shortening proves finite-order elements conjugate into factors. No geometric-finiteness or parabolic-rank conclusion is inferred.

The regular-closed Jordan-ball boundary argument passes open disjointness to avoidance of the opposite closed ball without forbidding contacts. All reduced sign patterns are checked. When first/last sign and initial base subgroup permit overlap, p=f^(first sign)(a) lies in the fixed input open ball and is omitted independently of all varying base coefficients. This proves faithfulness and rules out identity-convergent sequences without assuming an open gap, finite order of f, or a cyclic intersection hypothesis. Reduced powers give stable-letter independence and cyclic HNN reduction gives the torsion assertion. No full geometric combination clause is claimed.
